assumptions: J is an integer >=2 and h is a positive real duration. Fin J uses zero-based indices; source indices are1,...,J.
t_j=(h/2)(1-cos(j*pi/(J-1))), ell_j is the actual Lagrange cardinal polynomial on all these nodes. All j in Fin J are quantified, including both endpoints.

Weights are actual interval integrals against ordinary real Lebesgue measure. Polynomials are continuous and hence integrable on the finite intervals; these facts are proved, never supplied as premises.
units.statement: For every integer J>=2, every real h>0 and every j in Fin J, with t_i=(h/2)(1-cos(i*pi/(J-1))) and ell_j=Lagrange.basis univ t j, the actual momentum weight omega_j=integral_0^h ell_j(s) ds is nonnegative.

steps.title: Work with the actual extrema, keeping endpoint factors
steps.text: Put n=J-1>=1, theta_i=i*pi/n and c_i=1 at i=0,n and2 otherwise. Define C_n(a)=2 sum_(k=0)^n cos(ka)-1-cos(na). A finite sine telescope gives sin(a/2)C_n(a)=cos(a/2)sin(na). At all integer multiples m*pi/n with0<=m<=2n, C_n is2n at m=0,2n and0 otherwise. The interior sine factor is strictly positive, so division is justified. Negative differences use evenness.

steps.title: Derive the finite cardinal polynomial, rather than assume it
steps.text: The cosine product identity gives twice the product sum as C_n(a-b)+C_n(a+b). Hence P_i(x)=c_i/(2n)[2 sum_(k=0)^n cos(k theta_i)T_k(x)-1-cos(n theta_i)T_n(x)] has degree<=n and value1 at its own cos(theta_i) node and0 at every other node. Both endpoint factors and n=1 are included. Chebyshev T_k(cos a)=cos(ka) is a pinned Mathlib fact.

steps.title: Compute ordinary Lebesgue moments by an antiderivative
steps.text: For integer k different from ±1, F_k=T_(k+1)/(2(k+1))-T_(k-1)/(2(k-1)) has derivative T_k, using the polynomial derivative/U recurrence. The genuine FTC on[-1,1] yields I_k=integral T_k=(1+(-1)^k)/(1-k²). The exceptional k=1 integral is zero directly; I_0=2. Thus odd positive moments vanish, and even k>=2 give -2/(k²-1). No Chebyshev weighted measure or Gauss zeros are substituted.
steps.lean: F_hasDeriv; integral_T_formula; I_zero; I_one; I_odd; I_even

steps.title: Keep both parities in the strict absolute-moment budget
steps.text: For A_m=sum_(k=1)^m |I_k|, the even moments telescope since2/(4r²-1)=1/(2r-1)-1/(2r+1). Two-step induction proves A_m=1-1/(m+1) if m is even, and1-1/m if m is odd. It includes m=0, with A_0=0, and gives A_m<1 for every m.

steps.title: Integrate the actual finite cardinal polynomial and prove positivity
steps.text: Continuity supplies all interval-integrability conditions for finite-sum and subtraction linearity. The integrated bracket is B_i=2+2 sum_(k=1)^(n-1) cos(k theta_i)I_k+cos(n theta_i)I_n. Since |cos|<=1, B_i>=2-2 A_(n-1)-|I_n|>=2-2 A_n>0. Multiplying by the strictly positive c_i/(2n) proves integral_(-1)^1 P_i>0 for every actual node. The empty interior sum handles n=1.

steps.title: Identify the exact source basis and scale its actual integral
steps.text: Use x=1-2s/h. P_i(1-2s/h) has degree<=J-1 and the actual source cardinal values. The existing compiled coefficient producer supplies injectivity of the original t_i; polynomial interpolation uniqueness then identifies P_i(1-2s/h)=ell_i(s), with all natural/real J-1 casts checked. The genuine interval-integral affine substitution, including reversed extrema ordering, gives omega_i=(h/2) integral_(-1)^1 P_i>0 and hence the source nonnegativity conclusion. h>0 justifies the affine inverse.

units.lean_statement: Exact all-J, all-h source Lagrange polynomial Lebesgue integrals.
units.lean_proof: Finite cosine cardinal construction, polynomial FTC/moments, strict absolute budget and exact affine source identification; whole private implementation module covered by the public review.
